Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Rajagopalachar @ Rajagopalachari,
who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 26-06-2023, at about 5.30 p.m., the deceased Rajagopalachar @ Rajagopalachari was going towards his village Chaluvanahalli from Narasapura by riding a TVS Star City motorcycle bearing Reg. No.LA-07-R-7561, slowly, cautiously, on the correct side of the road.
When he reached near Chaluvanahalli Gate, on Bengaluru-Kolar NH-75 road, Kolar Taluk and District, the driver of the Kia Carens car bearing Reg.

No.TN-05-CK-9201 came from same direction i.e. from Narasapura side, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over his vehicle, went to the wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the motorcycle of the deceased from behind.
Due to the said impact, the deceased was knocked down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment and then he was admitted to Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and discharged from the hospital.
He developed severe illness and unbearable pain in the injuries sites and hence he was again being taken to Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote.
But, he succumbed to the said injuries on the way to the hospital.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Kolar Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- with interest.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, on 26-06-2023 at about 5.30 p.m., he was driving his car bearing No.TN-05-CK-9201 in a normal speed, cautiously, by observing all the traffic norms.

It was the deceased who was riding his motorcycle in a haphazard manner, without following proper traffic rules and suddenly slowed down his vehicle without any indiction on the main road, near Chaluvanahalli Gate, on Bengaluru-Kolar highway, he fell down from his vehicle and sustained injuries.

Further he has contended that, the car bearing No.TN-05-CK-9201 is insured with the respondent No.2 vide policy No.OG231021182500053242, valid from 24-01-2023 to 23-01- 2026 and he was holding valid driving licence to drive the same, at the time of accident.
If at all any award is passed by this Court in favour of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 is to be held liable to pay the same.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, the alleged accident has taken place on 26- 06-2023, whereas the claim petition has been filed on 05-03- 2024 i.e. after 8 months 9 days from the date of occurrence of alleged mishap.

There is an inordinate delay on the part of claimant in filing the present claim petition and it has not been filed with the time limit as stated in the provisions under Section 166(3)
of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Hence, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is barred by limitation and therefore, it cannot be entertained and not maintainable in the eyes of law and is liable to be dismissed.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.OG-23-1021- 1825-00053242 in respect of car bearing No.TN-05-CK-9201 and it was valid from 24-01-2023 to 23-01-2024 with respect to own damage liability and from 24-01-2023 to 23-01-2026 for third party liability, subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, exceptions and limits and endorsements of/to the policy, compliance of 64VB of Insurance Act.

Further it is contended that, the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-R- 7561 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmet, in a rash and negligent manner, without possessing valid vehicle documents and he had suffered the self accident.
The alleged insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver, who had no valid and effective driving licence.
Therefore, the insured has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action.
Further it is contended that, the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is necessary party to the proceedings to adjudicate the matter fully and finally.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper party, as the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is the necessary party to the proceedings.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed on this ground alone.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

13. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.5 spot mahazar and Ex.P.6 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 30 feet wide Bengaluru-Kolar NH-75 road, near Chaluvanahalli Gate, Kolar, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-05-CK-9201 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-R-7561 of the deceased.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.7 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further,
the investigation officer in his Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-05-CK-9201 and dashing the said vehicle to the motorcycle of the deceased and the deceased has succumbed to fatal injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-05-CK-9201 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Rajagopalachar @ Rajagopalachari in the said accident and the cause of his death.
15. No doubt, there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint by the complainant.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.

He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to the deceased,
there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
16. There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint stated in Ex.P.2 first information statement.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay in lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

23. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
24. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
25. Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 55 years.

To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Rajagopalachar @ Rajagopalachari, which is marked as Ex.P.19, wherein the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1968.
Admittedly, the accident has occurred on 26-06-2023.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 55 years.
It is averred in the petition that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, the petitioners have not produced any document to prove the avocation and income of the deceased.

The petitioners have deposed that, they have expended huge amount towards medical treatment and other charges of the deceased.
In order to prove the same, they have produced 162 medical bills and 7 ambulance bills, as per Ex.P.20 and 21.

towards medical expenses of the deceased.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,49,302/- towards the medical expenses.

The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
